prompt.context: Your client received a call last night and was given the opportunity to make a bid for the rights to Quentin Tarantino's next movie. She has 24 hours to make a bid.
prompt.question: How much should your client bid?

clarifying_info.q: What return threshold does the client require?
clarifying_info.a: The client requires a 40% return on investment.

clarifying_info.q: What kind of film is this?
clarifying_info.a: It is a low-budget film with no famous actors.

framework: Understand the objective: determine a maximum bid that satisfies the 40% return threshold
Estimate total revenues: box office revenue + additional revenue streams (DVDs, royalties, merchandising)
Estimate total costs: film production, marketing, distribution
Calculate profit and back into maximum bid = total profit / 1.4

questions.prompt: What factors drive box office success?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm MECE buckets: (1) Talent — famous actors, director reputation; (2) Film characteristics — special effects, 3D, genre, controversial content; (3) Studio capabilities — marketing strength, distribution network; (4) Timing — seasonal effects, competing releases. Bonus: out-of-the-box ideas such as special advertiser partnerships (positive) or explicit/controversial content (negative).

questions.prompt: How would you estimate film studio profits? Walk through revenues and costs.
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for the data needed. Revenue = box office; Costs = film + marketing + distribution (as % of revenue). Calculate profit step by step.

math.setup:
Box office revenue = # theaters × shows/week × weeks × seats/show × occupancy × ticket price
Costs = film cost + marketing cost + distribution cost (50% of revenue)
Profit = Revenue − Costs
steps: Revenue: 2,000 theaters × 5 shows/week × 10 weeks × 500 seats/show × 50% occupancy × $10/ticket = $250M
Film cost: $25M; Marketing cost: $25M; Distribution cost: 50% × $250M = $125M

questions.prompt: What are additional sources of revenue beyond box office? Incorporate them into the total profit calculation.
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm additional revenue streams: DVD sales, merchandising, royalties (video rentals via Netflix/Amazon Prime, Video on Demand via cable/airlines, movie channels such as HBO and Showtime). Interviewer then provides: DVD sales + royalties profits = $25M; merchandising profits = $25M.

math.setup:
Total profit = box office profit + DVD/royalties profit + merchandising profit
Maximum bid = total profit / (1 + required return)

questions.guidance: Recommendation should be succinct with: (1) summarizing statement, (2) supporting findings, (3) risks and next steps. See recommendation section.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors drive box office success?

categories.name: Talent
ideas: Director reputation and brand (e.g., Tarantino himself)

categories.name: Studio Capabilities
ideas: Distribution network and number of theaters

categories.name: Timing & Competition
ideas: Other major releases in the same time frame

categories.name: Out-of-the-Box
ideas: Special partnerships with advertisers for additional publicity
Social media virality or cultural moment

recommendation: Recommend the client bid up to $90M for the rights to Quentin Tarantino's next movie
This bid is supported by estimated total profits of $125M ($75M box office + $25M DVD/royalties + $25M merchandising), which meets the 40% return threshold ($125M / 1.4 ≈ $90M)
risks: Movies frequently run over budget; Tarantino's past track record may increase this risk
Competing releases at the same time could reduce box office occupancy below the 50% assumed
Other bidders may have different risk profiles or higher willingness to pay, affecting auction dynamics
Revenue estimates (especially merchandising and royalties) carry uncertainty for a low-budget film with no big-name actors
next_steps: Refine occupancy and revenue assumptions using comparable Tarantino films
Assess competitor bidders and their likely bid ranges
Stress-test the model with lower occupancy (e.g., 30–40%) and higher production costs
Iterate on the bid within the 24-hour window as new information becomes available
